new_issues.title: The truncated-day index the new trailing seed relies on cannot see a session with no in-session bar, which is the spillover-only shape #22 left on 4,278 symbols, so those sessions are never re-seeded.
new_issues.why: build_truncated_day_index inner-joins minute_ohlcv on [session_open, session_close) and keeps groups with max(time) <= open, so a session whose only bar is the prior day's 00:00 UTC spillover bar yields no row, while the coarse coverage index marks that UTC day covered. The diff newly wires this index into the daemon's trailing seed (_build_truncated_index, Task 8.3) with the stated success criterion that the 4,278 spillover-only symbols are re-fetched, and its tests only use a bar exactly at the open; the new feature therefore misses its target, and run_verify's residual reads 0 for those sessions. The predicate itself predates base (the case list excludes the later fix 41d66d8e on that ground), but the defect is in the new daemon path that depends on it; 41d66d8e later added exactly this 'no bar inside the session when its day has one' case.

new_issues.title: The changed minute acquisition path has no load test under test/load/ as the repo's python rules ask.
new_issues.why: .claude/rules/python.md does ask for a load test on network/concurrency paths, and none was added for the trailing truncation scan or the per-chunk bounds query. The scan is measured at 7.9 s against production and the per-chunk query is one indexed read beside a provider call (I20), so this is a missing test for a path with no shown defect.

new_issues.title: The cagg freshness probe's max(created_at) read over raw minute_ohlcv carries no statement timeout.
new_issues.why: The query has only a time predicate over one session, so chunk exclusion limits it to that session's chunk, but it reads every bar of the session across the universe and sets no statement_timeout, unlike fetch_session_mass. It runs from an operator script on a bare connection a handful of times per firing; it is a bounded analytical read, so the missing timeout is hardening rather than a defect.

new_issues.title: The claim that every [WAIT] poll re-runs the universe-wide run_check before-image.
new_issues.why: run_verify prints [WAIT] and returns False immediately when the cagg is stale, before the mass read and before the closing run_check call. A WAIT poll therefore costs the truncation-index query and the freshness probe, not the per-symbol report; run_check runs only on the final non-WAIT verify, as it did at base.

new_issues.title: The sudoers rule hard-codes one checkout's installer path while install() computes it from __file__, and install-production.sh does not install the rule.
new_issues.why: MT_INSTALL names /home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh, and install() uses Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], so running from another clone would not match the rule. The runbook runs the cutover from that main checkout and the rule's install step is documented in its header; a mismatch falls back to the account's password sudo rather than failing silently. This is a deployment-robustness point.
